ruling.recommended_action: Apply $3.74 voucher refund to rider (unexempted detour mileage × per-km rate) and record the driver's RD-1 shortest-route violation.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route 22:57–23:03 (+1.14 km). No rider consent message before the segment (chat [F10] contains only the two 22:40 pickup messages [F8][F9]); driver's post-trip 'GPS rerouted me' [F11] is not consent (RD-5, G11). No traffic incident on the optimal route [F14]; only speed band 3 [F12][F13], which is neither band 1 nor 2 and cannot exempt alone (RD-4(a)(b), G3). Counts under RD-1/RD-2.

Off-route 23:21–23:24 (+1.51 km, up to 985 m from optimal route). No rider instruction or agreement to this routing anywhere in the chat record [F10]; driver chose the route himself, so the deviation is not exempt under RD-3 or RD-5. No qualifying traffic cause [F12][F13][F14] under RD-4. Counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's assertion that 'nothing wrong with the fare' and that GPS rerouting excuses the deviation: a GPS suggestion is not a 'reasonable cause' under RD-4 without a traffic incident on the replaced optimal segment ([F14] shows none; band 3 [F12][F13] is insufficient per G3), and self-chosen rerouting without prior rider agreement is a violation of the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty (RD-1, RD-5).

Speed bands of 20–29 km/h (band 3) on East Coast Parkway [F12] and Airport Boulevard [F13] do not meet the band 1–2 threshold, and no incident falls within 300 m of the optimal route [F14]; therefore no segment qualifies as exempt.
